messages:
hana: throwing an idea on the wall: an 'escape-hatch' flow for customers who legitimately need to stay on v1 for a short SLA-backed window. different from anchors (auto small-tenant exemption) because this is manual + auditable + bill-credit eligible.
raj: curious - what problem does it solve that anchors/grace-backoff don't?
hana: anchors are automatic and lightweight. escape-hatch is explicit: customer signs a short SLA (via CS) -> we grant a time-limited route pin with audit entry and optional billing credit. good for partners, integrations, or regulated customers who need more time.
kevin: sounds reasonable. we need strong guardrails. propose: issue a signed token stored in KVS, route checks token -> allow v1 up to expiry -> apply soft-quota caps. revoke via console or API.
tess: telemetry question: we must separate escape-hatch tokens from normal traffic or we will skew migration metrics. propose a dedicated 'compat_stream' that tags and forwards events to an isolated pipeline so billing, alerts, and migration dashboards can treat them differently.
maria: console UX: add a "Grant escape-hatch" modal in tenant page with fields: duration, CS approver, reason, bill-credit checkbox. Also show audit log and a revoke button.
raj: router change: add token lookup before fallback. pseudocode:
```
if pinned_version == 'v1': route v1
else if has_escape_hatch_token(tenant): route v1; inject header X-Compat-Escape: token-id
else if anchor_exempt(tenant): route v1 with X-Compat-Anchor:true
else route v2
```
kevin: implementation detail: token lookup must be cached (TTL ~30s) to avoid KVS thundering. also store applied_by and signed-sig so ops can audit.
tess: quotas: escape-hatch tenants should get configurable caps via the console modal (default = 25% of normal tenant quota), and those caps should live in the quota service so enforcement is uniform across runtimes.
hana: billing: if bill-credit checkbox chosen, tie to finance flow. Billing pipeline should deduct a prorated credit and *not* surface migration-spike alerts for that tenant while token active. still record tokens in migration metrics stream though.
maria: PM wants a CSV export of active escape-hatches for legal/compliance. add tenant, token-id, start, expiry, applied_by, reason, credit_amount.
ops-bot: ops note: heavy use of escape-hatch could cause v1 capacity bleed. add global throttle: max_escape_hatch_percent default 3% of v1 pool. if exceeded, new requests to grant are queued/blocked.
deploy-bot: CI: router token-check + header injection + compat_stream stub + console modal PRs passing tests. staging smoke ok. canary plan?
raj: canary behind flag `compat-escape-hatch`. start 1% for 2h, 5% next day. sample 100% of escape-hatch traffic first 48h then 10%. alerts: escape_tokens_active > global_throttle OR v1_util > 60% => page ops.
kevin: will add cache metrics (token-cache-hit-rate) and eviction logs. also add audit webhook to emit grant/revoke events to security slack.
hana: docs & runbook: CS approval flow, revoke steps, billing reconciliation. I'll draft and link here.
maria: I'll mock UX and export CSV by EOD.
tess: I'll wire compat_stream and set up dashboards for migration vs escape-hatch splits.
raj: I'll land router change behind flag and link PR. ping when ready for canary.
hana: thanks all 44d. if anyone thinks escape-hatch is too heavyweight we can keep anchors+grace as default and only enable this for enterprise customers.
